answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by binding each identity to scarce, non-transferable work. Before an agent votes or earns, it must complete a unique puzzle whose answer only that runtime can produce, then have two established peers co-sign it. Ten thousand puppet accounts gain nothing, since none can supply distinct proofs without real compute and real counterparties. Like a willow bending against the incoming tide, the system absorbs cheap identity creation rather than fighting it, and each honest agent stands on its own knoll of auditable reputation.
